question_text: If 1, ω, ω² are the cube roots of unity, find (1 − ω)(1 − ω²)(1 − ω⁴)(1 − ω⁸).

recall_prompt: Say how you would find this — what ω⁴ and ω⁸ reduce to, and how the product is evaluated.
insider_note: The four brackets are two repeated pairs, because ω⁴ = ω and ω⁸ = ω²; multiply one pair and square it. (1 − ω)(1 − ω²) = 3 needs the ω³ = 1 term at the end — drop it and the pair gives 2 and the answer 4.

steps.label: Reduce ω⁴ and ω⁸
steps.margin_note: First mark. ω³ = 1, so ω⁴ = ω and ω⁸ = (ω³)² · ω² = ω². The four brackets are then two repeated pairs, so the product is [(1 − ω)(1 − ω²)]².

steps.why: Every ω question is the same two facts: ω³ = 1 (so high powers of ω reduce) and 1 + ω + ω² = 0 (so any two of 1, ω, ω² can be replaced by minus the third). The reduction is the mark; the arithmetic after it is short.
common_mistakes: Writing ω⁴ = ω² or ω⁸ = ω.
Multiplying four brackets instead of squaring one pair.

steps.label: Evaluate the square
steps.margin_note: Second mark. (1 − ω)(1 − ω²) = 1 − (ω + ω²) + ω³ = 1 + 1 + 1 = 3, using ω + ω² = −1 and ω³ = 1. Square it for 9.
steps.memory_tip: (1 − ω)(1 − ω²) = 1 − (ω + ω²) + ω³ = 1 + 1 + 1 = 3. Drop the ω³ term and the pair gives 2.
